events.text: ⏰ Online check-in is erroring — check in at the STL counter tonight. Seats are CONFIRMED (you're in the row 20 bulkhead — don't let the desk move you out of it). Bring Dr. Senol's printed letters and ask about a World Traveller Plus upgrade. TSA PreCheck is covered by Global Entry, so don't sweat what prints.
BA220 · STL → LHR · World Traveller
Overnight flight — arrives June 8 at ~11:24 AM (Terminal 5)

items.text: Final packing check: passports for all 4 (including Louise, age 5)
Charge all devices, download offline entertainment for overnight flight
Pack carry-on essentials: snacks, change of clothes, toothbrush — you land midday and go straight to the hotel
Light dinner before heading to airport. UberX picks up 7:20 PM → at STL ~7:36 PM, ~4 hrs before the 21:40 departure (you'll want the time — check-in is at the counter)
Kids' iPads loaded + headphones packed for 8-hr overnight flight
Wear the Hidden Disabilities Sunflower lanyards (all 4) from STL. Recognized at Heathrow, St Pancras/Gare du Nord, and Disneyland Paris — discreet, patient assistance at every checkpoint.

Refrigerated meds + syringes stay in carry-on (Meghan: Benlysta + GLP-1; Michael: Repatha). Keep Dr. Senol's letters printed AND on your phone. Declare medically-necessary liquids/gel packs at security — allowed over 100ml.
Michael's rescue inhaler within reach for the flight — not buried in the overhead bag.
Early/pre-boarding: ask at the gate — it's logged on the booking via the BA Accessibility call. Helps you get settled and stow the medical cooler.

Seats CONFIRMED — outbound you're in the row 20 bulkhead: Michael 20D, Louise 20E, Meghan 20F (extra legroom), Kenna one row back at 21K. Don't let online tools or the desk move you out of row 20. Return: Meghan 20F bulkhead, the other three together in row 21.
BA220 · STL → LHR · Departs 21:40, arrives ~11:24+1 · Terminal 5 (7h44m, tracking early)
World Traveller (economy). Booking ref: YUAD5K
Paid with 260,000 Avios + $1,083.86 in taxes/fees
Flight is ~7h44m. Meal service included. Try to sleep — you land midday and need to power through Day 1
✅ UK ETA approved for all 4 — have the confirmation emails on your phones at the gate.
✅ BA Advance Passenger Info complete for all 4 (passport + KTN on file).
Overnight flight with a 5-year-old: bring comfort items, tablet loaded with shows, noise-canceling if possible

events.text: Arrive LHR Terminal 5 (~11:24). Early check-in booked from 12pm!
🚄 Heathrow Express → Paddington (15 min)
Tube to Kings Cross. Check into Travelodge
WiFi code: TVLRTFRPK · Breakfast included all 5 mornings

⭐ Right by the hotel: Platform 9¾ + Harry Potter shop (King's Cross — the kids will love it), Granary Square fountains (1,080 jets — Louise will go wild on a warm afternoon), Coal Drops Yard, St Pancras. All a 5–10 min walk.
Early dinner — Pizza Union (fast, cheap, walk-in) is ideal for a tired arrival day; save Dishoom for a lunch another day (its dinner queue runs 30–60 min).

items.text: Have UK ETA confirmation accessible on phone for each passenger
Brush teeth, wash face before landing — you'll want to feel somewhat fresh
Have hotel address ready: Travelodge London Kings Cross Royal Scot
Immigration at T5 — can take 30-60 min. E-gates may work for US adults with ETA; kids under 12 use staffed desks
Heathrow Express: Pre-booked (ref 69d52862). Platform in T5 basement level. 15 min to Paddington
Paddington → Kings Cross: Hammersmith & City or Circle line → Kings Cross St Pancras (~20 min). Use contactless payment
Travelodge: Early check-in available from noon! Walk from Kings Cross station ~5 min
Jet lag will hit HARD, especially Louise. Power through until 7-8 PM local time to reset body clocks
Don't over-plan Day 1. Coal Drops Yard is a 5-min walk — perfect low-key exploring
Contactless payment works everywhere in London (Tube, buses, shops). No cash needed
Louise might crash mid-afternoon. Have a stroller or be ready for a hotel nap break
Travelodge WiFi code: TVLRTFRPK. Breakfast included all 5 mornings
Coal Drops Yard has great kid-friendly restaurants (Pizza Pilgrims, Barrafina)
St Pancras station next door has beautiful architecture — worth a peek even on arrival day
Kenna Oyster card: Buy at Paddington or Kings Cross Tube station (£7). Ask staff to add Young Visitor discount (50% off, 14 days). Kenna must be present. Louise rides free everywhere as under-11
Adults + transport: Apple Pay on your iPhones works on all London transport (Tube, buses, Thames Clipper). Just tap at the yellow readers. Auto-caps at daily rate. No Oyster card needed for adults

Cash: London is tap-everywhere — carry just £50–80. Paris needs more (~€100–150): the Metro will NOT take a bank-card tap, so buy a Navigo Easy card (€2) at Gare du Nord and load trips. Disney is card-friendly; ~€30–50 cash for tips.

Tipping: UK — a 12.5% service charge (if it's on the bill) legally goes to staff; otherwise ~10–12.5%. France — service is included ('service compris'); just round up or leave €1–2pp. Hotel housekeeping £1–2 / €2–5 a night (cash). Uber: no tip expected either country.
Data: T-Mobile gives 5GB/line then throttles to ~2G (too slow for maps). Lean on offline Google Maps + a backup Airalo/Saily eSIM, and turn off photo auto-sync on cellular. WhatsApp for calls/texts.

VAT refund: UK tax-free shopping is gone. France's détaxe only pays off on €100+ single-store buys, validated at the Gare du Nord PABLO kiosks when you leave Jun 16 — worth it only for a big purchase.

Delay safety net (no insurance): UK261 owes ~£520pp for a 3h+ BA delay/cancel PLUS meals/hotel — demand the care and keep receipts. Eurostar owes refunds/free rebooking; a missed Jun 16 return can still catch BA221 via the 12:12 train.

details.title: Emergency & Medical — tap if you need it

items.text: Emergency numbers: UK 999 or 112 · France 112 (any) / 15 (medical, SAMU) · Paris urgent house-call doctor SOS Médecins +33 1 47 07 77 77 · France on-duty pharmacy 3237.

Nearest ER: London → UCLH, 235 Euston Rd (10 min from the hotel). Disney → GHEF Marne-la-Vallée (+33 1 64 77 64 77). Central Paris → Hôtel-Dieu (by Notre-Dame), or the bilingual American Hospital of Paris.

Pharmacy: UK 'chemist' = Boots (King's Cross station ~7am–10pm; 24h at Leicester Sq). France 'pharmacie' = green cross; Val d'Europe (1 RER stop from Disney) is well-stocked. Kids' Tylenol = Calpol (UK) / Doliprane (France).
Paying (no insurance): UK A&E treatment is FREE — only hospital ADMISSION is billed to visitors. France = pay then keep the receipt. Get itemized bills for any care.

Lost / warm refrigerated med? Benlysta is fragile (discard if out >12h). Replace abroad via a private GP (London: DocTap King's Cross) or médecin (SOS Médecins) → local prescription; bring Dr. Senol's letter + a copy of the Rx. Disney First Aid refrigerates injectables in-park.
Meghan / long flights (APS): compression stockings, aisle access, water every hour, move every 2 hrs, skip alcohol — and confirm any clot prophylaxis with her doctor. Same care on long park days.

Louise + June heat at Disney: offer water every 15–20 min (don't wait for her to ask), SPF50, shaded breaks; watch for heat exhaustion. Disney rents wheelchairs/ECVs at the entrance (reserve ahead — June sells out).

events.text: 🏛️ St Paul's Cathedral (opens 8:30) — floor, the Quire & the Crypt (Nelson, Wellington, Wren). Book tickets online the night before: cheaper + a timed slot, Louise free.
⛪ Climb the Dome — all four of you: Whispering Gallery (257) → Stone → Golden Gallery (528 steps) for the best view in London. (Louise may want a carry up top.)
Cross the Millennium Bridge (dome behind you) → stroll the South Bank west toward the Eye, or hop the Uber Boat (Bankside → Eye pier).
Lunch on the South Bank near the Eye (Gabriel's Wharf, Royal Festival Hall, or Wahaca).
🎡 London Eye (30 min ride)
Cross Westminster Bridge → Big Ben & the Houses of Parliament (right on your path) for photos.
🦢 St James's Park pelican feeding at Duck Island Cottage (daily ~2:30 PM) — surreal, and Louise's favorite. Great playground in the park too.
🐎 Horse Guards '4 o'clock' Dismount (Whitehall) — armored Household Cavalry up close, almost no crowd.
Trafalgar Square — climb the lions & the fountains. National Gallery is free (open till 6) if you're still flying.
🍜 Dinner in Chinatown (5–10 min from Trafalgar) — saving Covent Garden for tomorrow's Matilda day.

items.text: 🎟️ Book St Paul's tickets ONLINE tonight — cheaper than the gate (~£25 adult, Kenna child rate, Louise free) and you get a timed slot. Opens 8:30, last entry 4 PM.
Save the London Eye e-ticket on your phone (Order #601617735) + a screenshot backup.
Showers are likely tomorrow — pack rain jackets + a layer. Indoor bailouts are all built in: St Paul's, the Eye's enclosed pods, the National Gallery.
Comfy shoes — the dome is 528 steps and there's good walking. A water bottle each. Quick Travelodge breakfast, then out the door for ~8:45 at St Paul's.

START — Travelodge → St Paul's (~8:45): walk 5 min to St Pancras, take Thameslink to City Thameslink (direct, ~5 min ride, every ~10 min), then a 5-min walk. Or a black cab/Uber straight to the cathedral steps (~£14, ~15 min, no stairs) — easy for four in the morning.

St Paul's → the Eye: cross the Millennium Bridge to the South Bank, then walk west ~25 min (Tate Modern, the Globe), OR hop the Uber Boat (Bankside Pier → London Eye/Waterloo Pier, ~15 min). Contactless taps for everything.
Afternoon is all flat & walkable: Eye → Westminster Bridge → St James's Park → Horse Guards → Trafalgar → Chinatown. Grab a black cab/Uber only to skip a leg.

END — Chinatown → Travelodge: Leicester Square is a 3-min walk from Chinatown → Piccadilly line direct to King's Cross St Pancras (~10 min, no change). With a tired Louise at night, a black cab/Uber is the easy call (~£14, door to door).
London Eye 1:00 PM is FIXED. Be at St Paul's by 8:45 so the dome + crypt don't run long — leave St Paul's by ~11:15 to make lunch + the Eye comfortably.
Pelican feeding is ~2:30 PM (runs to ~3). Head straight from the Eye across Westminster Bridge so you don't miss it — Big Ben photos happen on the way, no detour.
Changing of the Guard is NOT on Tuesdays — don't go looking for it. The 4 PM Horse Guards Dismount is your cavalry moment instead.
Dinner is Chinatown — Southbank Food Market is closed Tuesdays and Borough Market shuts at 5, and you're saving Covent Garden for Matilda tomorrow.
The dome payoff: the Golden Gallery (very top) is THE photo — 360° over the City. The Whispering Gallery on the way up is a fun trick: a whisper carries clear across the dome.
Pelicans: they've lived in St James's Park since 1664 (a gift from a Russian ambassador). Hand-fed mackerel at Duck Island Cottage — arrive a few minutes early for a good spot.
Horse Guards: the 4 PM Dismount (the 'punishment parade') dates to 1894, when Queen Victoria caught the guards slacking. Tiny crowd, big spectacle.

Access (fallback — Meghan's doing it all): if she ever wants them, St Paul's has a step-free North Transept entrance (floor + Crypt step-free) and the Eye gives a free carer ticket + FastTrack with a Blue Badge/PIP. Bring the doc just in case.

plan.intro: Tap a choice at each step to shape the day — picks stick and sync for both of you. Matilda at 2 PM is the fixed point.

options.label: Street magic + Neal's Yard
options.summary: Covent Garden's 'Magic Corner' runs world-class street magicians from 11 AM — they pull little kids into the tricks. Pair it with the rainbow Neal's Yard courtyard 2 min away.
options.travel: Piccadilly line: King's Cross → Covent Garden, ~12 min.

notes.text: Arrive ~11 for a full 30-min set; stand near the front so Louise gets picked.
Cash for tips: you've been cashless — many performers now take contactless/tap-to-pay, or break a £10 note for coins at any Tesco. Don't plan around it.

options.then: You're a 5-min walk from the Cambridge Theatre for Matilda.

options.label: Fashion loop for Kenna
options.summary: Seven Dials boutiques + vintage (Goldsmith, Size?) → Carnaby Street (Brandy Melville, Monki) → Liberty London (the Tudor building + the famous scarf hall).
options.travel: Piccadilly line to Covent Garden; it's all walkable up to Carnaby/Liberty (~10 min).

notes.text: Liberty's Tudor halls + scarf room are the most fashion-immersive free spot in London.

options.then: Loop back down to Seven Dials for the theatre.

options.label: Sir John Soane's Museum
options.summary: A Georgian house crammed with antiquities — walls that swing open to reveal hidden paintings, and an Egyptian sarcophagus in a candlelit crypt. Free and wonderfully weird.
options.travel: Piccadilly line to Holborn (~10 min), then a 4-min walk to Lincoln's Inn Fields.

notes.text: Go at the 10 AM opening — it's small and gets crowded. Allow 45 min.
Add Goodwin's Court nearby — a gas-lit 'Diagon Alley' cobbled passage, free.

options.then: Walk ~12 min to the Cambridge Theatre.

options.label: Seven Dials Market
options.summary: Covered food hall, ~20 vendors (Bleecker burgers, Pizza Pilgrims, dumplings) — 2 min from the Cambridge Theatre.

options.label: Rock & Sole Plaice
options.summary: London's oldest chippy (1871), 3 min from Covent Garden — proper cod & chips at tables out in the alley.

slots.label: 🎭 Matilda the Musical · Dress Circle Row A · Seats 23-26

notes.text: Arrive by ~1:35 (Cambridge Theatre, Seven Dials). Runs 2h40 — ends ~4:30. Chinatown's a 5-min walk after.

options.label: Chinatown dinner
options.summary: Gerrard Street is a 5-min walk from the theatre — dumplings, roast meats, bubble tea.
options.then: Home: Piccadilly line Leicester Sq → King's Cross (~10 min), or a cab.

options.label: Fairy Tales exhibition, then dinner by the hotel
options.summary: The British Library's immersive Fairy Tales show (costumes, puppets, pop-up books) is 5 min from the Travelodge — squarely Louise's world. Dinner at Coal Drops Yard after.
options.travel: Piccadilly line back to King's Cross, ~10 min.

plan.intro: Meghan's South Bank day. Optionally split the morning at County Hall (by the Eye): pick BOTH the Dungeon and Paddington and use the 👥 who-chips to split (e.g. Meghan + Kenna → Dungeon, Michael + Louise → Paddington — same building, reconvene at the riverside). Then walk east to Borough. Tap the stops that fit the mood; it's too much to do all.

options.label: Normal red double-decker (the smart pick)
options.summary: Hop a regular red double-decker (Route 91) from King's Cross and grab the top-front seats — the exact iconic bus Louise wants. Ride ~20 min to Trafalgar, then walk over Westminster Bridge to the Eye / County Hall.
options.cost: ~£4 (2 adult taps; Louise FREE, Kenna 50% w/ Young Visitor discount)
options.travel: Board at King's Cross St Pancras (Stop R). Contactless tap — under-11s ride free, no ticket.

notes.text: Same red double-decker as the tour buses, for pennies — and it drops you a short walk from County Hall.

options.then: Walk Westminster Bridge → County Hall (Dungeon / Paddington below).

options.label: Tootbus hop-on-hop-off tour
options.summary: Open-top sightseeing bus — board at Trafalgar, hop off at the London Eye for County Hall, then keep using the all-day pass (Borough, Tower, etc.). Add the 45-min live-guided Kids Tour — the real gem for a 5-year-old.
options.book: Book online (tootbus.com); Kids Tour sells out in summer
options.travel: Closest hop-on is King's Cross & St Pancras (Tootbus Green Route — right by the hotel), but it's a ~hourly connector: ride it to Trafalgar and switch to the main Yellow loop (London Eye stop for County Hall). Or Tube ~8 min to Trafalgar and board the frequent Yellow directly — also where the 45-min Kids Tour departs.

notes.text: Worth it as a tour + Louise's bus, not a 3-hr loop. Open top; lower deck is covered if it rains.

options.label: Skip the bus — just Tube it
options.summary: Tube to Waterloo (~15 min), 3-min walk to County Hall. Fastest, no fuss.

slots.title: Morning — County Hall (by the Eye), or straight to the river

options.label: London Dungeon
options.summary: A 90-min live-actor walk through London's dark history (Jack the Ripper, the Plague) — theatrical and darkly funny, designed for age 12+. Kenna's exactly the target age.
options.travel: County Hall, by the London Eye — Tube to Waterloo/Westminster (~12 min from King's Cross).

notes.text: It's scares-plus-comedy, not horror; actors don't touch you. ~90 min.

options.label: Paddington Bear Experience
options.summary: A 70-min immersive theatre journey from Paddington Station to 32 Windsor Gardens — gentle, magical, no scares. Age 4+; perfect for Louise.
options.travel: Same building as the Dungeon (County Hall) — start ~20 min after the Dungeon so the two parties finish together.

notes.text: Buggy park + loos; reviews love it for 5-year-olds.

options.label: Skip County Hall — straight to the river
options.summary: Head straight to London Bridge for the Golden Hinde / Borough Market below.

options.label: Golden Hinde galleon first
options.summary: Climb aboard a full-size Tudor galleon (Drake's ship) 2 min from Borough — three decks, cannons, captain's cabin. A real pirate ship.
options.travel: Thameslink St Pancras → London Bridge (~6 min) or Northern line (~12 min); 5-min walk to St Mary Overie Dock.

notes.text: Do it FIRST at 10 AM while Louise is fresh and before the market packs out.

options.then: Borough Market is right next door.

options.label: Straight to Borough Market
options.summary: Graze the stalls before the crowds build: Kappacasein grilled cheese, Bread Ahead doughnuts, Turnips chocolate strawberries.
options.travel: Thameslink St Pancras → London Bridge (~6 min); 3-min walk.

notes.text: Kappacasein's queue gets long — head there first.

slots.title: A delight along the river — pick one

options.label: Hays Galleria 'Navigators'
options.summary: A 60-ft kinetic bronze sea-monster ship in a Victorian glass arcade — bizarre and spectacular at kid height. 3 min east of the market.

options.label: Leake Street graffiti tunnel
options.summary: London's legal street-art tunnel under Waterloo — artists painting live, walls that change daily. Kenna's camera will love it.
options.travel: ~15-min riverside walk west toward Waterloo.
options.then: Loop back east toward Tate Modern.

options.label: REPLAY recycled playground
options.summary: A giant adventure playground built entirely from recycled materials, inside the Royal Festival Hall — pick up, build, wear, destroy. Louise-bait.
options.travel: On the South Bank by the Eye — ~12-min walk west.

options.label: Fashion & Textile Museum
options.summary: Meghan's pick — 'Paint! Pattern! Print!', the sisters behind Liberty's famous prints. Small, vivid, design-focused.
options.travel: 5-min walk from Borough Market down Bermondsey Street.

options.label: Tate Modern + Level 10 view
options.summary: Turbine Hall + the free Level 10 skyline view (better than paying for the Shard). Cross the Millennium Bridge for the St Paul's shot.
options.travel: ~15-min riverside walk from the market.

options.label: British Museum + Cartoon Museum
options.summary: Mummies, the Rosetta Stone, the Great Court — plus the tiny Cartoon Museum next door (free for kids, Kenna's kind of place).
options.travel: Tube to Tottenham Court Road / Holborn (~15 min), short walk.

options.label: Back to King's Cross / Coal Drops Yard
options.summary: Wind down near the hotel — Granary Square fountains, Coal Drops Yard, easy dinner. Good if everyone's spent.

plan.intro: Everything's a 5-minute walk apart in South Kensington. The NHM at 10 is booked — then tap your afternoon. (Pack for Paris tonight — 5:15 AM Eurostar!)

notes.text: Hintze Hall blue whale + the dinosaur gallery. Allow ~90 min. South Kensington.

options.label: Science Museum WonderLab
options.summary: A hands-on science playground 3 min from the NHM — Van de Graaff hair-raising, body-sized bubbles, live shows every 30 min.
options.travel: 3-min walk from the NHM along Exhibition Road.

options.label: Diana Memorial Playground
options.summary: A Peter Pan-themed adventure playground with a giant pirate galleon, in Kensington Gardens. Free.
options.book: Verify it's reopened the morning of (royalparks.org.uk)
options.travel: ~12-min walk through Kensington Gardens from the NHM.

options.label: V&A free galleries + lunch
options.summary: The V&A's free fashion, photography & Cast Courts (a giant plaster Trajan's Column!), plus its courtyard café for Louise's lunch/nap.
options.travel: 5-min walk from the NHM.

options.label: V&A: Schiaparelli
options.summary: The blockbuster surrealist-fashion show — Dalí's lobster dress, the skeleton dress, 100 garments. The fashion exhibition of 2026.
options.travel: Inside the V&A, 5 min from the NHM.

options.label: Design Museum: NIGO
options.summary: First UK retrospective of NIGO (BAPE / KENZO) — streetwear as culture, opening with his recreated teenage bedroom. The standout teen pick.
options.travel: ~15-min walk or short bus to Kensington High Street.

notes.text: Has a free permanent gallery + garden too.

options.label: Saatchi: The Sun & the Moon
options.summary: Immersive teamLab light installation + Luke Jerram's 6-metre sun — both kids equally dazzled.
options.travel: Tube/bus to Sloane Square, Chelsea (~15 min).

events.text: ⚠ Pack for Paris TONIGHT — 5:15 AM Eurostar wake-up tomorrow
Wake up. Walk to St Pancras (5 min)
🚄 Eurostar 9002 · Coach 10 · Seats 18,17,13,14
Arrive Paris Gare du Nord
Metro to Trocadéro → photos, then walk to tower entrance

⭐ Grab award-winning croissants at Maison Carton (2 min from Gare du Nord, opens 6am) for the train; at Trocadéro, the Belle Époque carousel spins with the tower right behind it (~€3 — Louise's photo).
🗼 Eiffel Tower · Summit by Elevator (4 tickets)
Lunch near Eiffel Tower
Metro → RER A to Marne-la-Vallée (~1 hr)
Check into Dream Castle Hotel

Kids: castle pool & water slide! Evening: dinner in Disney Village — OUT OF POCKET (the meal plan starts tomorrow at Art of Marvel). Annette's Diner or Rainforest Café are the easy kid picks; the Steakhouse takes reservations.

items.text: Bags packed by door. Alarm 5:15 AM. Clothes laid out
Eurostar tickets on phone. Ref: QRXPZK. Train 9002, Coach 10, Seats 18/17/13/14
Travelodge is 5-min walk to St Pancras — leave hotel by 5:30 AM latest
No hotel breakfast (too early). Grab pastries at St Pancras or eat on Eurostar

Leg 1: Walk to St Pancras (5 min). Aim to be there ~05:15 — Eurostar suggests 75 min ahead (60 with assistance); it's a quiet early Saturday but there are 5 stages: ticket → UK exit → security → French entry → board. Gates close 6:01. Use Eurostar Assist at Booth 5 for Meghan. Don't stop for coffee until you're past French control.
Leg 2: Eurostar 9002 · 06:31→09:57 Paris Gare du Nord. Security + UK exit + French entry checks before boarding
Leg 3: Gare du Nord → Trocadéro: Metro Line 4 → Line 6 (or Line 9). ~30 min
Leg 4: Eiffel Tower area → Disney: Metro to Châtelet, RER A to Marne-la-Vallée/Chessy. ~1 hour. ~€5/person
Dream Castle shuttle: Free from Disney bus station. Runs ~every 20 min
5:15 AM alarm with a 5-year-old. Have Louise's clothes and a snack ready to go
✅ Eiffel Tower tickets BOOKED! 4 tickets, Summit by Elevator, 11:00 AM entry. €101.00 (~$121). E-tickets sent via email — print or have on phone.

Arrive at Trocadéro by ~10:15 for photos, then walk to the tower for 11:00 entry. Allow 20–30 min in the security + elevator queue even with timed tickets. ♿ Summit accessibility: the very top is NOT permitted for guests who can't walk unaided (evacuation is stair-only) — if Meghan is using a cane / limited that day, staff may stop her at the 2nd floor (still spectacular at 115m). Have a Plan B; the 2nd-floor view works for everyone. Present her access pass at the West pillar for priority entry.
RER A to Disney: Validate your tickets! Fine for no validation is €50+
Watch belongings on Paris metro — tourist areas are pickpocket-heavy
